text:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> KD-721: kv-cache memory growth spike on prod-gpu-pool-3, severity: P1. Alloc failures observed.

eli (infra-oncall): I'm on it. Seeing lots of cudaMalloc errors in the logs and GPUs at 95% mem. Repro window: 23:14 - 23:28 UTC.

michael: logs look like repeated continuous-batching requests with huge prefix KVs being materialized. KV cache size jumped ~7x in 10m.

sasha: Confirmed. Customer-facing latency climbs and a handful of 502s on the embeddings route. Chart: kv_cache_bytes_total spiking, fragmentation metric ais_frag_rate up.

priyanka: Is this the same batch-config regression we saw in staging last week? We had a bad default change to BATCH_DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS that increased coalescing.

eli (infra-oncall): Possibly. Pulling last deploy. deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.14.3 -> rolled to prod-gpu-pool-3 at 23:00 UTC.

ops-sre: Dump from node-7:/var/log/redwood/serve.log.gz around 23:16:```[23:16:12] ERROR torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.02 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 29.30 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 28.34 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
[23:16:13] WARN kv_cache: arena_reserve_mb=256, arena_usage=92%, slab_count=1643, free_chunks=12
[23:16:14] WARN contbatch: queued=2048, batch_window_ms=180, avg_seq_len=520```

michael: Those contbatch queued numbers are huge. If each request caches prefix KV of ~100KB, 2000 concurrent leads to 200MB+ of frag-prone objects per node.

priyanka: Quick mitigation suggestion: reduce continuous-batching window and cap queued batch size to limit prefix caching. Two knobs: REDWOOD_CONTBATCH_MAX_QUEUED and REDWOOD_CONTBATCH_WINDOW_MS.

eli (infra-oncall): Agree. Pushing a hotfix to feature flags to set contbatch window to 40ms on prod-gpu-pool-3 only. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: flag-update: feature/contbatch-window -> set REDWOOD_CONTBATCH_WINDOW_MS=40 on pool=prod-gpu-pool-3 (change-id: fwu-9832).

sasha: After flag flip: KV cache growth rate reduced within 90s. But fragmentation still high; some nodes still hit alloc churn leading to OOMs.

ops-sre: We should also enable immediate KV slab compaction and lower arena_reserve_mb. Proposal: run compaction and set arena_reserve_mb=96 on affected nodes. That should free reserved memory and avoid PyTorch reserved blowouts.

eli (infra-oncall): Running compaction job now (one-off) across the pool: ``/usr/local/bin/kv-cli compact --pool prod-gpu-pool-3 --concurrency 4``

michael: While compaction runs, can we evict large-read-heavy customers behind a routing rule? We can route 10% of traffic to smaller/compatible model to reduce load.

priyanka: Created temporary routing policy: route tag=bulk-embeds -> fallback-model=rtd-embed-sm (lower memory). Applying to tenant set /customer-impact  (change-id: route-2187).

customer-success: Heads up — we saw brief errors for three enterprise customers. CS is notifying them with note: "Transient performance degradation and brief errors for embedding workloads; mitigation in progress."

oncall-bot: Incident bridge created: https://meet.redwood.com/incident/KD-721.

ops-sre: Compaction job completed on 6/8 nodes. Verified reclaimed ~18% of reserved arena memory on those nodes. OOMs dropped by 70% on those nodes.

eli (infra-oncall): There's still a noise floor on two old nodes (node-2, node-4) with a legacy allocator config (arena_split_threshold=1) — they are not behaving like the others. Suggest draining them.

michael: Initiating drain: ``kubectl cordon node-2 && kubectl drain node-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``. Doing node-4 next.

deploy-bot: node-drain job started (job-id: drain-1245). Expect pod reschedule within 3m.

priyanka: After drains, observed drop in fragmentation metrics and no new cudaMalloc errors for 12m. Load backpressure reduced.

ops-sre: Follow-up: we should push allocator tuning to default config: arena_reserve_mb=128, arena_split_threshold=64, enable_slab_reuse=true. This requires a small restart of runtime on the pool.

eli (infra-oncall): Propose a rolling restart with 1 node at a time, 10-minute cool down. I'll coordinate with platform windows. ETA start 00:20 UTC. Any objections?

sasha: No objections. Please include a canary and monitor kv_cache_bytes_total and cuda OOM logs.

customer-success: Customers acknowledged. They asked for ETA on fix; told them we expect full remediation within 2 hours and will provide a follow-up postmortem.

michael: Quick notes to preserve for postmortem: root cause appears to be an inadvertent batch-config change in 2026.03.14.3 that increased batching window and queue depth causing sustained cache prefix population. That drove fragmentation and caused PyTorch CUDA reserved memory to be insufficient, leading to OOMs. Contributing factors: two older nodes with legacy allocator settings, and lack of an automatic slab compaction trigger under high contbatch pressure.

eli (infra-oncall): Incident status: mitigated -> hotfix applied (contbatch window reduced, routing fallback applied, compaction run, nodes drained). Monitoring for 30m. Creating follow-up action items in KD-721: allocator-default-tuning, add auto-compaction trigger, guardrails on contbatch queue size.

ops-sre: Quick commands we ran for runbook (for notes):
```# set feature flag
redwood-admin flags set contbatch.window_ms 40 --scope pool:prod-gpu-pool-3
# compact slabs
kv-cli compact --pool prod-gpu-pool-3 --concurrency 4
# node drain
kubectl cordon node-2 && kubectl drain node-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# set allocator defaults (applied via configmap)
kubectl set env ds/redwood-runtime ARENA_RESERVE_MB=128 ARENA_SPLIT_THRESHOLD=64 ENABLE_SLAB_REUSE=true -n redwood```

eli (infra-oncall): I'll hand this to postmortem authorship: @michael + @priyanka. If anything regresses, page infra-oncall.

michael: grabbing it. Thanks everyone. 

sasha: marking incident as resolved -> status: mitigated; moving to postmortem. Reactions: :white_check_mark: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
